title: Creative Artifact Contract (contractVersion 1)
description: Machine-readable form of a Creative Artifact — the durable record of what was ACTUALLY produced from an approved Creative Intent. Answers 'what was created, where is it, what intent did it instantiate, what does it digest to, and is it approved for downstream consumption by its origin system' — never 'what should be created' (that is CreativeIntent's job, a separate contract this schema never extends or merges into). Carries a reference to the produced artifact, never the artifact's own bytes. A conformant instance says nothing about Offscript website-generation readiness; 'approved' here means approved by artifact.generation.sourceSystem only.

contractVersion.description: Contract major version. Must be in the reader's own supported set.

id.description: Stable identity for this artifact record. Opaque — no enforced format beyond non-empty. Distinct from artifactDigest: two artifacts with different id can legitimately share a digest (byte-identical regenerations), and an id never changes across the artifact's lifetime once assigned, while a regeneration always gets a NEW id (artifacts are immutable — see artifactDigest).

intentDigest.description: The CreativeIntent.digest this artifact instantiates — a REFERENCE, never recomputed or verified against a real CreativeIntent instance by this contract (that would require importing the intent package; this contract only carries the pointer). Multiple CreativeArtifact records may legitimately share the same intentDigest (one intent, several artifacts — e.g. desktop + mobile variants, or a static and an animated rendering). Never equal in meaning to artifactDigest, even if the two strings happen to collide.

artifactType.description: The kind of thing this artifact is. Closed vocabulary grounded in Repo B's actual current outputs (self-contained static creatives under Output/*.html, self-contained motion creatives under Motion/*.html — both single-file HTML, no separate image/video files are produced today) plus one deliberately generic 'asset' bucket for a future non-HTML artifact type not yet in evidence. Not a website-generation asset-type list — do not extend without new evidence.

location.description: A portable reference to the artifact's content — either a project-relative path (no drive letter, no UNC prefix, no leading '/', no '..' traversal segment) or a content-addressed 'content://sha256:<hex>' URI. Never an absolute machine-specific filesystem path. Structural portability is enforced by CreativeArtifactValidator, not by this schema's pattern alone (see src/artifact/location.ts) — the exact set of rejected shapes is richer than a single regex can legibly express, mirroring how this repository's other contracts (e.g. Creative Intent's 'trust' precondition) put judgment-heavy checks in code, not in the JSON Schema.

artifactDigest.description: sha256 content digest over the artifact's own referenced content (the bytes at `location`), computed by the producer with computeContentDigest(). Distinct from intentDigest by construction: it digests what was PRODUCED, not what was ASKED FOR. Two artifacts instantiating the same intent will normally have different artifactDigest values (different content); the same artifact regenerated byte-identically will legitimately produce the same artifactDigest under a new id.

createdAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of when this artifact record was created. Immutable once set.

generation.description: Structured metadata about how/where this artifact was produced. sourceSystem is required and is the ONLY field this contract treats as meaningfully interpreted (it is what approval.source must be read against) — everything else here is descriptive, not acted on by this contract.

sourceSystem.description: Names the system that produced this artifact (e.g. 'creative-generation'). Never 'offscript' or a Offscript track name — this field identifies an ORIGIN system, not a Offscript consumer.

runId.description: Optional identity of the generation session/run that produced this artifact, if the origin system has one.

generatorVersion.description: Optional version of the generating engine/skill.

methodologyVersion.description: Optional version of the design methodology applied (e.g. a Reference/_STYLE.md revision marker).

approval.description: The artifact's approval state AS RECORDED BY ITS ORIGIN SYSTEM ONLY. This is never equivalent to, and must never be interpreted as, a Offscript ReadinessState (src/project/readiness.ts) or a Offscript generation-admission decision — those are a structurally different, unrelated concept scoped to a whole Offscript project, not a single external artifact. A future explicit bridge may one day translate between the two; nothing in this contract performs that translation.

source.description: Names the system whose approval this status reflects (e.g. 'creative-generation'). Should match generation.sourceSystem in the common case; kept as a separate field because an artifact could in principle be approved by a system other than the one that generated it.

evidence.description: Optional free-text or reference pointing at the origin system's own approval evidence (e.g. a log line, a note). Never the full evidentiary record itself — a pointer, not a copy.

validation.description: Optional. Summarizes an origin-system validation/quality-gate result WITHOUT duplicating the full report (e.g. Repo B's Visual Proof Validation / 15-item Quality Bar) inline — reportDigest references it instead. Absent means the origin system has no validation concept for this artifact type, not that validation failed.

validator.description: Identity of what performed the validation (e.g. 'creative-generation/visual-proof-validation').

reportDigest.description: sha256 reference to the full validation report, if one exists as durable content. Never the report body itself.

provenance.description: Opaque, audit-only metadata beyond what `generation` structurally captures. Carried verbatim; never interpreted by any conformant reader. Same shape/role as Brief.provenance and CreativeIntent.provenance.

$comment: additionalProperties is true at the top level (forward-compatibility, matching brief.schema.json and creative-intent.schema.json) but false inside generation/approval/validation, since those are small, fully-enumerated structured objects this contract itself interprets — an unrecognized key there is more likely a mistake than a forward-compat extension. Enum values stay closed everywhere: an unrecognized artifactType/approval.status/validation.status is always a fatal structural error, never a warning.
